Westgold Resources Sets 500,000 Oz Annual Output Goal
By Rhiannon Hoyle
Westgold Resources said Wednesday that it aims to raise annual gold output to roughly 500,000 troy ounces before the end of this decade, while also potentially reducing mining costs.
The Australian gold producer said it is targeting output of between 385,000 and 425,000 ounces in the year through June 2027, compared to 387,000 ounces last fiscal year.
It expects fiscal 2027 all-in sustaining costs of between 2,980 Australian dollars, equivalent to US$2,151, and A$3,380 an ounce. That compares to A$2,841 an ounce last year.
By fiscal 2029, Westgold said it expects to produce between 460,000 and 510,000 ounces of gold, at a cost of between A$2,640 and A$3,000 an ounce.
The plan is underpinned by investments in Westgold's largest mines and Murchison processing capacity, the company said.
It expects to spend between A$450 million and A$480 million on growth projects in fiscal 2027.

"The capital program reflects a deliberate decision to prioritize Murchison investment and utilize Westgold's strong balance sheet, improving reserve confidence and growing mining inventories to invest ahead of production," said Chief Executive Wayne Bramwell.
He said fiscal 2027 will be the peak investment year under the three-year plan and that Westgold's organic growth would not come at the expense of shareholder returns.
